questions.q: What will the foreigners do to Babylon?
questions.a: They will come and destroy Babylon.

questions.q: What type of attack will come on Babylon’s army?
questions.a: A surprise attack will come so quickly that Babylon’s soldiers will not have time to put on their armor. The attackers will destroy the army and the people.

questions.q: What does Yahweh remind his people of?
questions.a: Yahweh reminds them that even though his people sinned he is still their God and he has not abandoned them.

questions.q: What does Yahweh tell the people of Israel to do?
questions.a: Yahweh tells his people to run, so they will escape the punishment coming to Babylon.

questions.q: What will happen to Babylon?
questions.a: It will fall and be destroyed.

questions.q: What did Yahweh use Babylon to do to the nations?
questions.a: He used it to make them drunk.

questions.q: What will the Israelites do because Babylon will not be healed?
questions.a: The Israelites will leave and go to their land and tell others in Zion that Yahweh has forgiven them of their sins.

questions.q: Who is going to march into battle against Babylon because Babylon destroyed Yahweh’s temple in Jerusalem?
questions.a: The armies of Media and Persia are going to destroy Babylon.

questions.q: What has Yahweh sworn he will do to the rich people of Babylon?
questions.a: Yahweh will raise a battle cry against them. Their end has come.

questions.q: What happens when Yahweh speaks?
questions.a: He brings thunder, rain, lightning, and wind to come upon the earth.

questions.q: What has Yahweh done by his power, wisdom, and understanding?
questions.a: He has made the earth, set it in place, and stretched out the heavens.

questions.q: Will making idols satisfy people?
questions.a: No, idols can do nothing for them. They are worthless.

questions.q: Who is the God of Israel?
questions.a: He is the one who created everything. His name is Yahweh.

questions.q: What did God say Israel was?
questions.a: God said Israel was his war hammer, his weapon for battle.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say to the people in Babylon?
questions.a: Yahweh says he will repay the people for all the evil things they did in Jerusalem.

questions.q: What will Yahweh do to Babylon because of how they plundered people all over the earth?
questions.a: Yahweh will completely destroy Babylon, and no one will ever live there again.

questions.q: What is Jeremiah to tell the nations of Media and Persia?
questions.a: These nations are to summon their armies and prepare to attack Babylon.

questions.q: What is Yahweh’s plan against Babylon?
questions.a: Yahweh’s plan is to make the land of Babylon a wasteland with no inhabitants.

questions.q: How will the Babylonian warriors respond to the battle against them?
questions.a: The warriors will remain confused in their strongholds because places of escape will be blocked, and the city will be set on fire.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say Babylon is like?
questions.a: Babylon is like a threshing floor during the time of harvest.

questions.q: What do the people of Jerusalem want Yahweh to do to the people of Babylon?
questions.a: They want Yahweh to cause the Babylonians to suffer like they suffered under King Nebuchadnezzar.

questions.q: What is Yahweh’s response to the Israelites?
questions.a: He will plead their case and bring vengeance on Babylon. He will make her springs dry and make her a wasteland where no one lives.

questions.q: What is Yahweh going to do to the people of Babylon?
questions.a: He is going to prepare a different kind of feast where they become drunk with wine and then are all slaughtered.

questions.q: What kind of place will Babylon become?
questions.a: Babylon will become a place of ruin among all nations.

questions.q: What will Yahweh do to the god Bel?
questions.a: Yahweh will punish Bel and make the people of Babylon give back the offerings that were given to Bel, and the walls of Babylon will fall.

questions.q: What does Yahweh tell his people who are in Babylon to do?
questions.a: He tells them to run and save their lives from all the violence that will be in the land.

questions.q: What happens that causes the heavens and earth to rejoice?
questions.a: The heavens and earth will rejoice because Babylon is destroyed by an army from the north.

questions.q: What does Jeremiah tell the Israelite people to do?
questions.a: They are to get out of Babylon, return to Jerusalem, and turn back to Yahweh.

questions.q: What had the Israelites heard about Yahweh’s house?
questions.a: They had heard that foreigners had entered the holy places of Yahweh’s house.

questions.q: What does Yahweh tell the people that he will do?
questions.a: He tells them that he will send armies to destroy Babylon.

questions.q: What do the people hear from Babylon?
questions.a: They hear a shout of distress as Yahweh destroys Babylon.

questions.q: What will happen to everything that the nations try to do for Babylon?
questions.a: It will all be useless.

questions.q: Who was King Zedekiah’s chief officer?
questions.a: Seraiah was his chief officer.

questions.q: What did Jeremiah write in a scroll?
questions.a: Jeremiah wrote all the disasters that were going to come to Babylon.

questions.q: What were Jeremiah’s instructions to Seraiah?
questions.a: Jeremiah told Seraiah that when he arrived in Babylon he was to read all the words on the scroll, tie a stone to it, and throw it into the Euphrates River.

questions.q: What was written on the scroll?
questions.a: Yahweh made a declaration that Babylon will be destroyed, have no inhabitants, and become a permanent wasteland.

questions.q: Why was Seraiah to throw the scroll in the river?
questions.a: When he threw the scroll in the river, the people would understand that Babylon will sink like the scroll because of the disaster Yahweh is sending on her.

questions.q: What were Jeremiah’s instructions to Seraiah?
questions.a: Jeremiah told Seraiah that when he arrived in Babylon he was to read all the words on the scroll, tie a stone to it, and throw it into the Euphrates River.

commentary.text: Babylon's doom; God's controversy with her; encouragements from thence to the Israel of God. (Jer. 51:1-58) The confirming of this. (Jer. 51:59-64)

Jer. 51:1-58 The particulars of this prophecy are dispersed and interwoven, and the same things left and returned to again. Babylon is abundant in treasures, yet neither her waters nor her wealth shall secure her. Destruction comes when they did not think of it. Wherever we are, in the greatest depths, at the greatest distances, we are to remember the Lord our God; and in the times of the greatest fears and hopes, it is most needful to remember the Lord. The feeling excited by Babylon's fall is the same with the New Testament Babylon, Rev. 18:9,19. The ruin of all who support idolatry, infidelity, and superstition, is needful for the revival of true godliness; and the threatening prophecies of Scripture yield comfort in this view. The great seat of antichristian tyranny, idolatry, and superstition, the persecutor of true Christians, is as certainly doomed to destruction as ancient Babylon. Then will vast multitudes mourn for sin, and seek the Lord. Then will the lost sheep of the house of Israel be brought back to the fold of the good Shepherd, and stray no more. And the exact fulfilment of these ancient prophecies encourages us to faith in all the promises and prophecies of the sacred Scriptures.

Jer. 51:59-64 This prophecy is sent to Babylon, to the captives there, by Seraiah, who is to read it to his countrymen in captivity. Let them with faith see the end of these threatening powers, and comfort themselves herewith. When we see what this world is, how glittering its shows, and how flattering its proposals, let us read in the book of the Lord that it shall shortly be desolate. The book must be thrown into the river Euphrates. The fall of the New Testament Babylon is thus represented, Rev. 18:21. Those that sink under the weight of God's wrath and curse, sink for ever. Babylon, and every antichrist, will soon sink and rise no more for ever. Let us hope in God's word, and quietly wait for his salvation; then we shall see, but shall not share, the destruction of the wicked.
